Listen to this article Share The Founder and President of the All Africa Music Awards (AFRIMA), Mike Dada, has been appointed to the Advisory Board of the African Collaborations Group (ACG).
Dada, who founded AFRIMA in 2014 in partnership with the African Union Commission, has played a significant role in promoting African music and culture globally. The awards platform is broadcast in more than 84 countries.
He also serves as Vice President of the African Union’s Pan-African Congress, where he led the development of the AU’s Plan of Action on Culture and Creative Industries, adopted by African Heads of State in 2023.
According to ACG, Dada’s appointment will strengthen its efforts to integrate sport and entertainment through the development of bankable sport and entertainment districts across Africa.
The organisation said his experience in cultural leadership, policy development and the creative economy would contribute to its vision of building sustainable ecosystems for Africa’s sport and entertainment industries.
Commenting on the appointment, ACG Founder and Executive Chairman, Nicolas Pompigne-Mognard, described Dada’s experience in continental cultural development and policy leadership as a strategic asset to the organisation.
